sn45.34:3.1: These verses also occur in the context of the seven awakening factors ([sn46.17:2.1]()), the tenfold path ([an10.117:2.1](), [an10.118:3.1]()), the ten ways of skillful deeds ([an10.169:3.1](), [an10.170:2.1]()), and as independent verses ([dhp85]()–89).
sn45.34:5.1: While the text has the singular _dhamma_ here, the commentary explains it by way of the contrast between “dark” qualities and “bright” qualities, which are typically in plural. And indeed, the Sanskrit parallels of this verse have the plural form. See Norman’s note on [dhp87]() in his *The Word of the Doctrine*.
sn45.34:5.2: _Bhāvetha_ here is a rare reflexive form for the third person optative singular, agreeing with _pariyodapeyya_ below.
sn45.34:5.3: The Pali for “home” is _oka_, which I elsewhere disambiguate by rendering as “bastion”.
sn45.34:7.2: For “awakening factors” the Pali has _sambodhiyaṅga_, which is a different spelling of _sambojjhaṅga_, familiar from the “seven awakening factors”.
